children: Triumph released the inaugural "

" report, a freight market analysis that suggests the trucking industry is entering a new era defined not by the availability of capacity, but by the availability of capacity that can be deployed with confidence.

Drawing on transaction-level data from the Triumph Network, one of North America's largest freight transaction networks, the "Triumph Mile Marker" report identifies an emerging shift toward defensible capacity. In this environment, the challenge is not only finding trucks and drivers, but determining which transportation providers can be deployed with confidence.

"For years, discussions about capacity centered on whether trucks and drivers existed," said Ben Volkwyn, executive vice president, head of enterprise data and intelligence for Triumph. "Increasingly, the question isn't whether capacity is available. It's whether capacity is trustworthy."

While freight markets have historically been shaped by cyclical shifts in supply and demand, the report suggests the industry may be experiencing a structural change. Regulatory oversight, carrier vetting practices and risk-management requirements are becoming larger factors in determining which carriers can effectively participate in the market. As a result, the lowest-cost option may not always be the preferred option, creating new opportunities and challenges for brokers, carriers and shippers alike.
The report highlights four trends that may reshape how brokers, carriers and shippers evaluate market conditions in the months ahead.
Not all brokers are experiencing the market the same way

Transaction data trends reveal meaningful differences in performance across broker segments, suggesting that business model, customer mix and operational flexibility are becoming increasingly important market differentiators. The report explores how different broker cohorts are responding to changing freight conditions and where opportunities may be emerging.
Traditional margin metrics may not tell the whole story

While many freight businesses continue to face pressure on a per-load basis, the report that rising transaction volumes may be contributing to stronger overall financial performance, even when traditional margin metrics remain under pressure.
Scale can be both an advantage and a vulnerability

The analysis examines how larger organizations and smaller organizations are benefiting from different competitive advantages today's market environment, challenging long-held assumptions about who is best positioned to succeed as market conditions evolve. Larger brokers have recently seen increased volume growth but also greater exposure to margin pressures when buy rates rise faster than contracted sell rates.
The data may be signaling changes before they reach the headlines

According to Triumph's analysis, enforcement activity, carrier verification requirements and broader regulatory developments appear to be influencing freight market behavior in ways that become visible in transaction data before they are reflected in conventional market narratives. The report examines how these factors may be affecting capacity availability and market dynamics.
The report suggests the transportation industry is entering a new phase in which capacity is increasingly evaluated through the lens of compliance, risk and operational readiness.

"Triumph Mile Marker" is the first in an ongoing series of freight market analyses from Triumph examining emerging transportation trends through transaction-level data.
About Triumph

Triumph (NYSE: TFIN) is a transportation-focused financial and technology company that delivers payments, factoring, banking and intelligence solutions designed to simplify and modernize freight transactions for brokers, carriers, shippers and factors. The company develops technology and financial products that improve operational efficiency, increase transparency and security in transactions, and expand access to working capital across the transportation industry. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, Triumph's portfolio includes Triumph, LoadPay and TBK Bank.

Through Triumph Intelligence, the company transforms the scale and operational depth of the Triumph Network into actionable freight market intelligence. Built on transaction-backed data from a network touching approximately 65% of brokered freight and supporting more than $40 billion in annual carrier payments, Triumph Intelligence provides pricing, capacity, volume, margin and market trend insights that help transportation companies make more informed business decisions.
